chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Who replaced McRae in Cab's band
summary: Al Gibson replaced him, and Cab later asked for another tenor, so McRae got Sam "The Man" Taylor.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Now, we're getting ready to go to the coast, and I decided I didn't want to go. So I sent to New York and got a tenor player.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
We had (inaudible) on the other tape, I think. (Inaudible).
Al Gibson replaced me. And Al Gibson --
Al Gibson was a tenor player we used in a lot of rock and roll dates around New York.
At that time. He played a lot of rock and roll dates for (inaudible).

And they went to the coast the next day for about two or three months and they came back. And so Cab asked me could I get him a tenor player. So I say, "Yeah, I know a fella." So I went up and got Sam "The Man" Taylor. Now Sam "The Man" Taylor at that time was playing on a lot of rock and roll dates. He had played on a lot of dates.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
And he really became famous after he -- He worked with Cab for a long time. Then he came back the rhythm and blues was coming in. And that's Sam made his name -- doing that.
